ROOT CAUSE + FIX: MPSGraph native SDPA silently corrupts attention when scores [heads,seq,seq] crosses 2^31 ELEMENTS. Boundary measured exactly: 56 heads, seq 6192 clean / 6193 broken. Broken heads -> near-uniform attention (no error/NaN/out-of-range); broken set grows from both ends of head range (int32 wraparound). Fix: head-chunked SDPA gated at heads*seq^2 > 1.9e9; below the gate the graph is byte-identical. Validated in standalone probe (0/168 spike spots broken to seq 7995) then in the model: 124f/5.175s clip clean (YAVG 114.2) in 14.2 min, and the 1582.7 s encode blowup cured to 0.388 s (same root cause, planner-level). make test 1769 ok; 22f reference still md5 886b40d10c5a83fb01393a4c62bdfcbd through fix + CLT->Xcode toolchain switch.

context_notes: The through-line of the last two sessions: every wrong conclusion came from a counter measured at the wrong boundary (root-gpu as a total; stream thread-time subtracted from a wall; random-data SDPA error looking mild because uniform attention mimics correct near-uniform softmax). Each was corrected by a cheaper measurement: reading weights beat generating; a planted spike beat random data; the exact 6192/6193 boundary named the mechanism. Bit-identity (md5 886b40d10c5a83fb01393a4c62bdfcbd) held through counters, the SDPA fix, and a full toolchain switch — it is the invariant that makes everything else trustworthy.
